title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 127
paragraphs: When Xerxes reached Therma, he established the army there. The encampment occupied no less than the following stretch of coast: starting from the city of Therma and from Mygdonia, it extended as far as the rivers Lydias and Haliacmon, which form the boundary between Bottiaea and Macedonia by mingling their waters into one and the same stream. In these places the barbarians were encamped; and of the rivers listed, only the Cheidorus, flowing from Crestonian territory, proved insufficient for the drinking of the army and ran dry.
